candidates.title: Count open and urgent tickets

demandEvidence.chore: Count open tickets and identify how many meet an urgent category.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Can your native n8n workflow count the open tickets, then find how many of those are urgent?

ease.reason: A count-and-flag mock can use sample ticket rows; this discussion gives no data format or implementation reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small service team may value a queue summary; the request does not establish payment for AI.

feasibility.reason: A four-week sample-data counter is narrow, but urgency rules and ticket access are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable count can run on supplied rows; a person must define urgency and verify results.

evidence.reason: The fresh request names counting open tickets and finding urgent ones, but gives no frequency or rules.

candidates.reason: Experiment: operator supplies fictional ticket rows as input; a manual run counts open rows and flags a proposed urgency label; compare with hand-counted results, with a person defining urgency and reviewing every flag. No attached source supports live ticket integration; mean 4.6 is below threshold.
